texts.preamble: Manish R vs Maheshwar Reddy Y on 22 December, 2025 Kabc020635052024 Before The Court Of I Addl. Small Causes Judge & Acjm & Motor Vehicles Accident Claim Tribunal, Bengaluru. (Scch-11) Dated This The 22Nd Day Of December - 2025 Present: Sri.Narendra.B.R., B.Sc, L.L.B. I Addl.Small Causes Judge & Acjm & Member - Mact Mvc No.7175/2024
texts.facts: This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident. 2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 15.03.2024 at about 09.00 to 09.15 a.m., he was traveling on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HS- 1565, as a pillion rider, from Tumakur side towards Akshaya College side and when he reached in front of MAR Swimming pool, Arakere, Tumakuru - Koratagere SH-33 Road, Tumakuru District, a Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-04-TX-9855, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the motor cycle. Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, he was shifted to Sridevi Hospital, Tumakuru and then shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent huge amount towards hospitalization, medical expenses, conveyance, food, nourishment and other incidental expenses. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was studying final year Diploma at Akshaya Polytechnic College, Tumakuru and earning a sum of .30,000/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability. The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver. The respondents, being the owner and insurer, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. 3. In pursuance of notice, both the respondents have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statement. 4. In the Written Statement, the respondents denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically. The respondents also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident. Further respondents contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed. Further contended that the driver of the lorry has driven the lorry in slow manner, to extreme left side of the road by following traffic rules, at that time the rider of motorcycle namely Kiran, driven the same at high speed in a negligent manner and hit the lorry. Further contended that at the time of accident the driver of lorry by name Manoj was very experienced in driving and he was having valid and effective driving license to drive the lorry. The respondent No.1, the owner of the said lorry, insured his lorry with respondent No.2 and at the time of accident, the policy of said lorry is in force and also the said lorry is having road permit to transfer the goods . The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant. Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition. 5. 2nd respondent, in the written statement, contended that the alleged accident is said to have taken place on 15.03.2024 but reported to the police on 16.03.2024 and there was delay in reporting the alleged accident to the police. Further respondent no 2 admitted the aspect of issue of insurance policy vide No.61120731230100000035 valid from 29.04.2023 to 28.04.2024, in respect of lorry belonging to 1st respondent and contended that the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy. Further the alleged accident was due to negligence of the rider of motor cycle who was unmindful of traffic and movement of vehicles on road without following lane discipline Manish R vs Maheshwar Reddy Y on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64515664/ 2 and giving way to the oncoming vehicles, suddenly moved to the middle of the road and dashed to the lorry. Further contended that the rider of motor cycle had no valid and effective driving license to ride the motor cycle and was not wearing safety helmet while proceeding on motor cycle. Further the driver of insured lorry also had no valid driving license authorizing him to drive the lorry at the time of alleged accident. The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant. 6. On the basis of above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following: ISSUES 1. Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 15.03.2024 at about 09.00 to 09.15 a.m., infront of MAR swimming pool, Arakere, Tumkur, Koratagere SH-33 Road, Tumakur District, when petitioner was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HS-1565 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-04- TX-9855 by its driver? 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom? 3. What order or award? 7. In order to prove the contention of the petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bengaluru as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed evidence of his side. The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.2, first information statement. On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information statement, friend of petitioner by name Shivakumar S/o Narasappa has lodged complaint with police on 16.03.2024 pertaining to the accident occurred on 15.03.2024. The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC and U/s.134(A&B), 187 of M.V.Act. In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle. The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle. Ex. P.1 12. The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar and spot sketch, which are marked as Ex.P.3.
texts.arguments: 14. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner. The respondents contended that the rider of motorcycle was also negligent and same has resulted in accident. But, the respondents have not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to substantiate the said contention. i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment. In order to prove the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner produced Wound certificate issued by Sridevi Institute of Medical Sciences & Research Hospital marked at Ex.P.6. The said document discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature. The petitioner also furnished Ex.P.7 - Discharge Summary issued by Hosmat Hospital, which discloses the aspect of availing treatment by petitioner for the injuries sustained by him in the accident. Further, the petitioner examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P15 & 16 documents. PW.2/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability and assessed the disability to the right lower limb at 63% and to the whole body at 21%. On consideration of the materials placed before the Tribunal, compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards Pain and Suffering. (ii) Towards Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses. The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital. The petitioner has produced Medical bills amounting to .6,39,256/- marked at Ex.P.9 and medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.13. The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said document. PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also, nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited. The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence. The respondents not furnished satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the medical bills furnished by petitioner. (v) Towards loss of income during treatment:- The petitioner contended that he was studying final year Diploma at Akshaya Polytechnic College, Tumakuru and was also earning a sum of .30,000/- per month was running a stationary shop at Tumkuru. The petitioner has not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that he was earning .30,000/- per month. (vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:- The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital and sustained permanent disablement. The petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., who was working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bengaluru as PW.2. Hence, future earning Manish R vs Maheshwar Reddy Y on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64515664/ 7 capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under : Annual Income before accident : (.16,500/- x 12) = .1,98,000/- Loss of future earning p.a. (10% of prior annual income) = .19,800/-. Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 18 Loss of future earnings - (.19,800/- x 18) = .3,56,400/-. The petitioner is entitled for .3,56,400/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
